title: Volume 0 · Driving the Desk Like an Operator
subtitle: Lessons 1–10: find any document, filter a list into a tool, build a report in a minute and hand the view to a team
outcomes: Navigate to any DocType or document in three keystrokes rather than a menu tree
Turn a list view into a per-role tool with filters, columns and saved views
Build a defensible report in Report Builder and say when Script or Query Reports are needed
Teach an operator the three habits that stop keyboard-and-menu time being the bottleneck
Hand a saved view to a team knowing how user permissions change what it shows

slides.title: One search box over every DocType and every document
bullets: The bar at the top of the Desk searches DocTypes, documents, reports and settings from one field
Two letters of a doctype and Enter opens the list, which is faster than any menu path you can memorise
Typing a document name or a customer name jumps straight to the record, not to a search results page
It also runs commands such as new sales invoice, so the whole Desk keys off this one control
Teach it first and stop drawing menu trees on whiteboards; they go stale, the search box does not

rows: Click the search bar or press the focus shortcut
Caret in the global search field
DocTypes and commands starting with Sal are listed
A New Delivery Note command appears

slides.notes: Operators lose more time to navigation than to data entry, and the search box is the single biggest win you can hand them in five minutes. But say the honest caveat out loud: shortcuts and exact wording differ between Frappe versions, so teach the habit of searching rather than a specific keystroke, and point people at the Help menu for their own version.

slides.title: Lists are the real interface, not the forms
bullets: Every DocType has a list view that filters, sorts, selects and exports without opening a single document
Filters combine with Add Filter, and each one narrows without destroying the previous state
Sorting by modified date answers the question 'what changed yesterday' faster than any report
The row count at the bottom is your arithmetic check before you trust a total
Most client questions — what is outstanding, what is late, what changed — are list questions, not form questions

rows: Open Sales Invoice from the search bar
List view with the default columns
Only overdue invoices remain, count updates
Add Filter: Company, equals, Seri Murni
The set narrows again, both filters shown
The list widens back without losing the other
Read the count at the bottom
Number you can reconcile against a report

slides.notes: The list view is where the client will live, yet training usually skips it in favour of forms. Spend the time here: filters that stack, sorting by modified, and the record count at the bottom. When someone says a report is wrong, the first thing you do together is reproduce their question as a filtered list, because the list shows its working and the report does not.

slides.title: A saved filter is a tool the whole team uses
bullets: Any working filter combination can be saved with a name and reappears in the sidebar for everyone
Name it for the job, not the query: Dispatch – today reads better than status equals not billed
Saved filters respect permissions, so a storekeeper sees the filter but only their own warehouses
Marking one as the default for a role turns the list view into a purpose-built work queue
This is standard configuration, so it survives upgrades and needs no customisation

rows: Set as default for the role
Saved filter menu, Set as default

slides.notes: This is the cheapest piece of value in the whole project and almost nobody does it. A saved filter named for the shift, with a default, means the dispatch clerk opens the system and is already looking at their work. Say clearly that it is configuration, not customisation: no code, no upgrade risk, and it can be renamed or removed when the job changes.

slides.title: Show the four columns that matter and act on many rows
bullets: Columns can be added, removed and reordered per list, and the choice is remembered per user
Selection checkboxes unlock bulk actions: submit, cancel, assign, or delete for drafts only
Export to Excel or CSV respects the current filters, which is how you hand data to an accountant
Bulk submit is legitimate for batches of invoices; bulk cancel is not a substitute for thinking
The column set is part of the saved filter, so a saved view carries both the rows and the fields

rows: Only filtered rows in the file
Select a submitted row, try delete

slides.notes: Show the export to the accountant in the room and you will win that person over immediately: a filtered list that leaves as a spreadsheet is how most Malaysian finance teams still work between systems. Pair it with the warning that the export is a snapshot, not a report, so nobody starts reconciling last month against an old download.

slides.title: A defensible report in one minute
bullets: Report Builder takes one DocType, a few columns, filters and a group-by, and saves as a report anyone can run
It is the right answer for turnover by customer, spend by supplier and stock value by warehouse
Group-by with a sum column gives a total that ties back to the list view count and the ledger
Save it with a name the business would use, then add it to the workspace so people can find it
If the question needs joins across DocTypes or scripted logic, it stops being a Report Builder job

rows: Builder form with DocType, columns, filters
Fields from that doctype become available
Group by Customer, Sum on Grand Total
One row per customer with a total
Report is runnable from the search bar

slides.notes: The point of this lesson is not the builder, it is the discipline of proving a number: group-by sum, then compare the grand total against the same filter in the list view. When the two agree, the client can defend the report in a meeting. When they disagree, you have found a filter mistake before the client has, which is the whole job.

slides.title: Report Builder, Query Report or Script Report
bullets: Report Builder is client-maintainable: columns, filters, group-by, no code, survives upgrades
Query Report is a saved SQL statement for a developer, quick to write and quick to break
Script Report is the supported path for logic, permissions and formatting that SQL cannot express
The functional consultant's job is to specify the question and accept the cheapest tool that answers it
Anything a client can maintain themselves should never become a customisation you own

rows: Aging by bucket with custom logic
Ask whether the question is real

slides.notes: Say the governance point plainly: every custom report is a thing you will be supporting for years, and every Report Builder artefact is a thing the client can change on a Tuesday. Push questions towards the cheaper tool, and only accept a Script Report when the logic genuinely cannot be expressed otherwise. Then make sure the requirement is written down in the UAT script.

slides.title: Three habits that beat any menu map
bullets: Search instead of navigating: the awesome bar reaches every screen the menu tree buries three levels deep
Save the view you use daily, as a named filter with a default, so the first screen is already the work
Keep the browser at one hundred percent zoom so columns do not collapse and totals stay aligned
Learn one shortcut per week from the Help menu rather than a printed list nobody keeps
Refresh before you report a bug: a stale tab is the most common false alarm in a go-live week

rows: Two letters plus Enter reaches the list
All columns visible, no horizontal scroll
Help menu lists them for this version

slides.notes: Resist handing out a printed sheet of shortcuts; it is out of date by the next upgrade and nobody keeps it. Give the habit instead: search for what you need, save the view you use every day, keep the zoom sane, and check one new shortcut a week in the Help menu. Then model it in every demo you run, because operators copy what they see.

slides.title: You know the amount and the customer, not the number
bullets: Search by customer name in the list filter, then sort by date to narrow to the week you remember
Amount filters accept ranges, so between 1,300 and 1,400 finds an invoice you only half recall
The global search also matches document names, so a partial number such as 0007 is enough
Once found, the Connections tab shows what was made from it, which is usually the next question
Teach this instead of letting people scroll a year of invoices looking for a familiar figure
slides.notes: This is the everyday question a client will ask you in month two, standing at your desk with a number in their head and no document reference. Show them that the answer is a filter, not a trawl. The Connections tab then answers the follow-up, which is always what happened to it afterwards.

slides.title: Saved views and permissions, together
bullets: A saved filter is shared, so a view built for dispatch is visible to anyone allowed to see that doctype
User permissions narrow the rows inside the view, so the same filter shows different data per person
Test the view as a restricted user before you call it done, otherwise the first demo surprises you
Name views after the role that owns them, and delete the ones nobody uses at each review
This is the cheapest handover artefact you can leave behind: named, permission-aware work queues

rows: Fewer rows for the restricted user

slides.notes: The trap is building a beautiful view as the administrator and never testing it as the person who will use it. User permissions change the rows, not the filter, so a view that looks perfect for you can be empty for dispatch. Always sign in as the restricted user before you show it, and write the view name into the handover pack.

slides.title: Fifteen minutes that make a new starter productive
bullets: Search, filter, save, export: four skills that cover ninety percent of everyday Desk work
Show the search box, one filtered list, one saved view and one export, then have them repeat it back
Give them their own saved view on day one, named for their job, so the system starts useful
Point at the Help menu for shortcuts and at you for anything that looks wrong after a refresh
Write the induction into the handover pack so the client can run it without you

rows: Fifteen minutes blocked in the calendar
Search to a list, then filter it
Save a filter named for their job
Spreadsheet opens with the same rows
Ask them to find one document by amount
Note the session in the handover pack

slides.notes: This is where navigation training pays for itself: fifteen minutes per starter, delivered by the client, with no consultant in the room. The induction belongs in the handover pack precisely because it is repeatable. If you leave the client able to teach search, filter, save and export, you have removed the most common reason people quietly go back to spreadsheets.

lab.title: Lab · Turn the Desk into three purpose-built work queues
steps: From the awesome bar, open the Sales Invoice list in three keystrokes and note the default columns
Filter to overdue invoices for Seri Murni, add Outstanding Amount and Due Date, and sort by amount
Save that view as Collections – overdue, set it as the default and note where it appears in the sidebar
Build a Report Builder report grouping submitted invoices by customer with a sum of grand total
Run the report and reconcile its grand total against the same filter applied in the list view
Export the filtered list to CSV and confirm the file contains only the filtered rows
Create a restricted user limited to Main Warehouse and confirm the saved view shows fewer, not different, rows
Repeat the exercise for Purchase Order as Procurement – this week, then write both view names into the handover pack
lab.done: Three named views exist, one is a role default, the Report Builder total reconciles with the filtered list count, the export matches the filter, and the restricted user sees a narrowed version of the same view.

quiz.question: What is the fastest reliable way to open an unfamiliar DocType's list in the Desk?
options: Navigate the module sidebar until the doctype appears
Type two letters of the doctype into the awesome bar and press Enter
Open the Setup workspace and search the DocType list
Use the browser's back button until the list appears
quiz.why: The awesome bar searches DocTypes, documents, reports and commands from one field. It is also version-stable in behaviour, unlike memorised menu paths, which move between releases.

quiz.question: A dispatch clerk needs to open the system and immediately see their own work. What do you build?
options: A Script Report restricted to their role
A saved filter named for the job, set as their default view
A new workspace with only their doctypes
A user permission that hides all other doctypes
quiz.why: A named saved filter with a default turns the list view into a work queue, is pure configuration, survives upgrades, and respects user permissions so each person sees their own rows.

quiz.question: When does a requirement stop being a Report Builder job?
options: When more than five columns are needed
When the question needs joins across DocTypes or logic SQL cannot express
When more than a hundred rows are returned
When the client wants to export the result
quiz.why: Report Builder handles one doctype, its columns, filters and a group-by. Cross-doctype joins and computed logic need a Query or Script Report, which is a development artefact you will maintain.

quiz.question: You saved a view as administrator and it looks right. Why must you test it as a restricted user?
options: Saved filters are not saved until another user opens them
User permissions narrow the rows inside the view, so it may be empty for them
Restricted users cannot see saved filters at all
The default filter only applies to the user who created it
quiz.why: Saved filters are shared, but user permissions filter which records a person may see. The same view can look complete to you and nearly empty to the storekeeper restricted to one warehouse.

quiz.question: A client reports that a total is wrong. What is the first thing you do together?
options: Rebuild the report as a Script Report
Reproduce the question as a filtered list view and compare the record count
Reconcile against the General Ledger
Ask them to send a screenshot of the report
quiz.why: A list view shows its filters and its row count, so it shows its working. Reproducing the question there finds a filter mistake in a minute, before you start questioning the ledger or the report.

memory.spine: Search, filter, save, share: the Desk is navigated by one search box and made useful by saved views.

device.label: Search, filter, save, share
expansion: Search: two letters in the awesome bar beats any menu path you can memorise
Filter: stack conditions in a list view until the question is answered
Save: name the view for the job and make it the default for that role
Share: permissions narrow the rows, so test the view as the restricted user
Export last: a filtered export is a snapshot, never a report to reconcile against

cards.q: Which control reaches every DocType, document and report from one field?
cards.a: The awesome bar at the top of the Desk. Two letters and Enter open a doctype list; a document name jumps straight to the record.

cards.q: What makes a saved filter more useful than a custom report?
cards.a: It is configuration, so it survives upgrades, respects user permissions and can be changed by the client without a developer.

cards.q: Why will the same saved view show different rows to two users?
cards.a: Saved filters are shared, but user permissions restrict which records each person may see, so the row count differs by role.

cards.q: When is Report Builder the wrong tool?
cards.a: When the question needs joins across DocTypes or logic that SQL cannot express. That is a Query or Script Report, and you will maintain it.

cards.q: What is the fastest way to prove a report total is right?
cards.a: Reproduce the same filter in the list view and compare the record count and the total. The list shows its filters; the report hides them.

trap.what: You build a perfect default view as administrator, demo it, and the dispatch clerk says it is empty on their login.
trap.why: User permissions filter the rows inside a saved view. Always sign in as the restricted user, or create one, before declaring the view finished.

narration: Operators lose more time finding things than typing them, so Volume zero continues with the interface itself. One search box at the top of the Desk reaches every DocType, every document, every report and a set of commands, which is faster and more durable than memorising a menu tree that moves between versions. The list view is the real interface: filters that stack, columns you choose, sorting by modified date, a record count at the bottom, and selection checkboxes that unlock bulk actions and exports. Take a filter combination that answers a real question, name it for the job, set it as the default for a role, and you have built a work queue that costs nothing to maintain and survives every upgrade. Remember that saved filters are shared while user permissions narrow the rows, so always test a view as the person who will use it. For anything needing joins or logic, Report Builder stops and a Script Report begins, and that is a decision to write down, because it becomes something you support.
